account:
Today I read my appointments and attended morning office business and the mill inspection. The mill stall held 77 hay bales; I removed nothing. I have now reached home for noon lunch, with council letters at thirteen, tea at the neighbour's cottage at fifteen, office at sixteen thirty, and the approved great-hall inspection at eighteen still ahead.

The unusual business is the secrecy around the hall preparations. This morning I heard Freight say both entrances were closed, request that an open shutter be checked, and say they would keep everything quiet until eighteen. That coincides with my scheduled builder's lighting and table inspection. It may simply be preparations for that inspection, perhaps something meant to be revealed then, but I do not know. The secretary has not established what Freight is preparing and had not found the builder to notify them. I asked for an accurate update and said office access must not change without my approval.

There are also repeated reports of a 'bridge or port change' discussed at the bakery. Townsfolk name the baker, innkeeper, neighbour, Freight and builder in differing accounts, but nobody has explained an actual change or its purpose. I crossed the bridge successfully on my way to the mill and returned west without a reported obstruction. These reports remain unverified; I cannot yet connect them to the hall preparations. Reports that the baker carried a sack of bread do not by themselves establish anything unusual.
